questions.q: The correct order of reactivity of alkyl halides towards ethanolic ammonia is:
questions.explain: Reactivity follows leaving-group ability of the halide ion: the weakest C–X bond (C–I) reacts fastest, so RI > RBr > RCl.

questions.q: Which condition makes the primary amine the major product when an alkyl halide is heated with ethanolic NH₃ in a sealed tube?
options: A large excess of the alkyl halide
questions.explain: With a large excess of NH₃, each R–X molecule is far more likely to meet NH₃ than the amine already formed, which limits over-alkylation. Excess R–X pushes the reaction towards the quaternary salt.

questions.q: Which halide does NOT give an amine when heated with ethanolic NH₃ at about 373 K in a sealed tube?
questions.explain: In chlorobenzene the C–Cl bond is strengthened by resonance with the ring, so it resists nucleophilic substitution unless strong electron-withdrawing groups are present ortho or para.

questions.q: Benzyl chloride is treated with ammonia and the product is then treated with two moles of chloromethane. The final product is:
questions.explain: Ammonolysis gives benzylamine, C₆H₅CH₂NH₂, and two CH₃Cl molecules alkylate the nitrogen twice to give C₆H₅CH₂N(CH₃)₂. N,N-Dimethylaniline is a trap: the nitrogen is on the CH₂, not on the ring.
